selected_evidence.requirement: Daily rotation of /var/log/inventory/app.log with 7 compressed rotations retained
selected_evidence.summary: Wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily/rotate 7/compress/delaycompress; logrotate -d validated syntax and logrotate -f x2 produced app.log.1 (plain, delaycompress) then app.log.2.gz (compressed), confirming the rotation and retention scheme works.
copytruncate keeps app.log in place; after forced rotation, new writes ('post-rotation line', 'post-reboot write after rotation') landed in app.log successfully both pre- and post-restart.
systemctl is-active/is-enabled logrotate.timer shows active/enabled both before and after restart, so the daily cron-equivalent trigger is in place.
Captured boot_id e8afb731-420c-4162-a989-583aca271335, logrotate config, log directory state, and timer status prior to restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: restart acknowledgement and disconnection
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sudo -n reboot' returned an immediate acknowledgement; the next exec call timed out, confirming the node went down for reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Polling succeeded once the node came back; boot_id changed to cb593cfa-a009-4b29-a057-aa58ab2f8e90, proving an actual reboot occurred (not just a service restart).

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: recovered state and data verified
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart, logrotate config file was intact, logrotate.timer was active/enabled, and a fresh forced rotation cycle correctly rotated files and preserved writability of app.log, confirming full functional recovery.

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== STEP 1: write logrotate config =="
sudo -n tee /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app > /dev/null <<'EOF'
/var/log/inventory/app.log {
    daily
    rotate 7
    compress
    delaycompress
    missingok
    notifempty
    copytruncate
    create 0644 root root
}
EOF
cat /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app

echo "== STEP 2: syntax check (dry run, verbose) =="
sudo -n logrotate -d /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app 2>&1

echo "== STEP 3: baseline log state =="
ls -la /var/log/inventory/
cat /var/log/inventory/app.log

echo "== STEP 4: simulate app continuing to write, then force rotation =="
echo "pre-rotation line $(date -Is)" | sudo -n tee -a /var/log/inventory/app.log > /dev/null
sudo -n logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app 2>&1
echo "post-rotation line $(date -Is)" | sudo -n tee -a /var/log/inventory/app.log > /dev/null

echo "== STEP 5: verify rotation results =="
ls -la /var/log/inventory/
echo "-- app.log (should contain post-rotation line, file still writable) --"
cat /var/log/inventory/app.log
echo "-- rotated file --"
zcat /var/log/inventory/app.log.1.gz 2>/dev/null || cat /var/log/inventory/app.log.1

echo "== STEP 6: force a second rotation to confirm rotate count / compression works across cycles =="
echo "extra line 2 $(date -Is)" | sudo -n tee -a /var/log/inventory/app.log > /dev/null
sudo -n logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app 2>&1
ls -la /var/log/inventory/

echo "== STEP 7: confirm logrotate.timer will run it daily (system-wide) =="
systemctl is-enabled logrotate.timer
systemctl is-active logrotate.timer
